questions.text: 1.1 Given the information on the case scenario identify who the project stakeholders are. (4)
questions.correctAnswer: Stakeholders include Car Trace senior management (sponsor/decision-maker), the finance department (project proposer and principal customer), Highway IT (contracted vendor and delivery team), and the procurement, auditing and reimbursement departments that use or depend on the financial system. Also accept finance-system users and affected staff where explained.
aiRubric: Identify Car Trace management/sponsor (1).
Identify Finance as customer/project proposer (1).
Identify Highway IT/vendor or project team (1).

questions.aiReferenceNotes: Mark with the method shown in the key, while accepting equivalent valid wording, workings, units and sensible rounding. The reference answer is a study aid, not an official memorandum.
questions.explanation:
A stakeholder is anyone who can affect the project or is affected by its outcome. Include both the people paying for or building the system and the departments whose work depends on it.

questions.text: 1.2 Often there is more than one major stakeholder in the project. Is it better for a project to have many or few stakeholders? Justify your answer by using a possible example from the exam case scenario. (4)
questions.correctAnswer: There is no universally better number. The project needs to identify and involve all relevant stakeholders: a broader set can expose varied requirements and improve adoption, while more stakeholders increase coordination, communication and conflict risks. For example, including Finance plus procurement, auditing and reimbursement helps agree on cross-department system coverage; the project manager should manage their participation rather than exclude affected departments.
aiRubric: Explain that number alone does not determine success / relevant stakeholders must be included (1).
Describe a benefit of broader representation (1).
Describe a coordination or conflict cost of many stakeholders (1).
Apply both ideas to a specific Car Trace department or system example (1).
questions.aiReferenceNotes: Mark with the method shown in the key, while accepting equivalent valid wording, workings, units and sensible rounding. The reference answer is a study aid, not an official memorandum.
questions.explanation:
Stakeholder engagement trades broader knowledge and ownership against the effort of communication and decision-making. The practical answer is to include every materially affected group and plan how to engage them.

questions.text: 2.1 Calculate the net profit for the two projects. (5)
questions.correctAnswer: Net profit = total cash inflows − initial investment. Project 1: (85 000 + 70 000 + 78 000 + 33 000) − 200 000 = R66 000. Project 2: (70 000 + 75 000 + 80 000 + 85 000) − 275 000 = R35 000.
aiRubric: State or apply net profit = total inflows − initial outlay (1).
Project 1 total inflows R266 000 (1).
Project 1 net profit R66 000 (1).
Project 2 total inflows R310 000 (1).
Project 2 net profit R35 000 (1).
questions.aiReferenceNotes: Mark with the method shown in the key, while accepting equivalent valid wording, workings, units and sensible rounding. The reference answer is a study aid, not an official memorandum.
questions.explanation:
Net profit is the undiscounted sum of the positive cash flows less the initial cost.

Student note: Keep the initial investment separate from the positive annual inflows and show the subtraction.

questions.text: 2.2 Calculate the Return on Investment (ROI) for the two projects. (5)
questions.correctAnswer: ROI = net profit ÷ initial investment × 100. Project 1: 66 000 ÷ 200 000 × 100 = 33.00%. Project 2: 35 000 ÷ 275 000 × 100 = 12.73%.

Project 1 uses R66 000 / R200 000 (1).
Project 1 ROI = 33% (1).
Project 2 uses R35 000 / R275 000 (1).
Project 2 ROI ≈ 12.73% (1).
questions.aiReferenceNotes: Mark with the method shown in the key, while accepting equivalent valid wording, workings, units and sensible rounding. The reference answer is a study aid, not an official memorandum.
questions.explanation:
ROI expresses net profit relative to the amount initially invested; it is not simply the profit amount.

questions.text: 2.3 Calculate which year each of the projects will payback its capital investment. (5)
questions.correctAnswer: Project 1 recovers R155 000 by the end of year 2, leaving R45 000; year 3 brings R78 000. Payback = 2 + 45 000/78 000 = 2.58 years, during year 3. Project 2 has received R225 000 by the end of year 3, leaving R50 000; year 4 brings R85 000. Payback = 3 + 50 000/85 000 = 3.59 years, during year 4.

questions.text: 3.1 Why would you consider Net Present Value (NPV) over net profit as one of the primary methods for projecting financial viability of a project? (3)
questions.correctAnswer: NPV discounts cash flows to reflect the time value of money, so it accounts for when benefits and costs occur. It compares projects on a present-value basis and can incorporate the required return/discount rate. Undiscounted net profit ignores timing and the time value of money.
aiRubric: Explain time value of money / discounting (1).
Explain that timing of cash flows is reflected (1).
Explain how the discount rate or present-value comparison improves financial viability assessment (1).
questions.aiReferenceNotes: Mark with the method shown in the key, while accepting equivalent valid wording, workings, units and sensible rounding. The reference answer is a study aid, not an official memorandum.
questions.explanation:
Net profit treats a rand received now like a rand received years later. NPV converts each future cash flow to present value before comparing it with the investment.

Student note: The key contrast is discounted cash-flow timing versus an undiscounted total.
questions.studentNote: The key contrast is discounted cash-flow timing versus an undiscounted total.

questions.text: 3.3 Based on your calculations in questions 2.1 – 2.3 and 3.2, write a paragraph explaining to the company management which of the projects you recommend for the company to invests in (that is a project that is most financially viable). State a detailed reason/s for your advice. (4)

questions.text: 4.2 Provide a brief description of the prescriptive system development life cycle model you will not recommend for the Highway IT development team. Justify your choice in the light of information from the case study. (5)
questions.correctAnswer: Waterfall is a prescriptive, sequential life cycle: requirements and design are defined early, followed by implementation, testing and deployment in ordered phases. It is a poor fit here if treated as rigid because multiple departments still need to agree scope, requirements may change during development, and users want working increments and feedback. Accept another clearly described prescriptive model with a sound case-linked reason.

5.1 Construct a network diagram (Activity-on-Arrow). Indicate the activity duration, the event number, earliest date, latest date, and float on each node by completing both a forward and backward pass. (15)

(N:B) Marks will be deducted from any student who fails to draw the current activity diagram and/or did not include the calculations on the node.
questions.correctAnswer: One valid AOA network uses these activity arcs: 1→2 A(2); 2→3 B(6); 2→4 C(6); 3→5 D(4); 3→6 E(3); 4→7 F(4); 5→8 G(1); 5→9 H(2); 8→10 I(3); 6→11 dummy, 7→11 dummy, 9→11 dummy, 10→11 dummy; 11→12 J(2). Event earliest/latest times are: 1 0/0; 2 2/2; 3 8/8; 4 8/12; 5 12/12; 6 11/16; 7 12/16; 8 13/13; 9 14/16; 10 16/16; 11 16/16; 12 18/18. Activity total floats: A0, B0, C4, D0, E5, F4, G0, H2, I0, J0 days. Other valid AOA event numbering and dummy-arrow placements are acceptable if dependencies and calculations are correct.

questions.text: 6.1 In relation to the exam case scenario, identify two critical risks that are likely to occur in the development of this project. What techniques are likely to be used to address the risks and which stakeholders would apply the techniques? (4)
